newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian army urges Moslem rebels to surrender.
newsitem.headline: Algerian army urges Moslem rebels to surrender.

text.p: The Algerian army is calling on grassroots Moslem rebels to break the "satanic hegemony" of their commanders and surrender to the authorities to join the ranks of the "sincere sons of Algeria".
The call is being handed out to motorists at roadblocks and a copy of it was printed by the Algerian newspaper Liberte on Tuesday.
"The homeland needs you. Regain consciousness and rejoin the sincere sons of Algeria, your true brothers and your sole family," the appeal said.
The military, which has been fighting Moslem fundamentalist rebels for more than five years, issued the call ahead of Algeria's June 5 parliamentary elections.
Thousands of rebels gave up after a multi-candidate presidential election in 1995, won by President Liamine Zeroual, who pledged clemency to rebels who broke ranks with the guerrillas.
Zeroual's government had adopted a clemency law early in 1995 guaranteeing amnesty for rebels who had not committed murder or economic sabotage and reduced sentences for those involved in killings.

The army call, declaring that the guerrilla movement was doomed, reminded the rebels of massacres of children, women and elderly and how "luxurious" was the life of their commanders, apparently with the aim of spreading division in their ranks.

"The time has come for you, lost young Algerians, to question yourself and recognise that you are on the wrong path and to meditate over the manner you have been misled and the reasons which have taken you to follow these criminals," it said.
Algeria plunged into violence in early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.

About 60,000 people have died in the five years of strife pitting Moslem guerrillas -- most of them young -- against government forces. Thousands of civilians have been caught up in the conflict and killed.
